title: sse: fix streaming chunking & framing for partial JSON, delimiter ordering, and token boundaries
author: Priya Nadar
description:
Motivation: Customers and SDKs (especially OpenAI-compat clients) observed truncated/invalid JSON when consuming SSE streams from Redwood. Root causes identified: 1) partial JSON objects split across chunk boundaries were not reassembled consistently by the SSE emitter, 2) delimiter ("

") insertion rules caused event/data tokens to be emitted in an order that some clients treated as separate events, and 3) tokenizer boundaries (sub-token flushes) produced mid-json flushes that broke partial-json handling. This PR fixes framing and chunking to make streaming robust across token boundaries and compatible with common OpenAI streaming expectations.

What this changes (summary):
- Implement a small stateful buffer in the SSE emitter that ensures partial JSON payloads are coalesced before emitting a data event unless the stream is explicitly flushed by the model/runtime. The buffer is bounded and has a defensible flush policy to avoid infinite buffering.
- Change delimiter ordering rules so that event/data fields and the terminating double-newline are emitted in a consistent sequence (data: ..., delim: "\n\n") to match OpenAI-compat consumers.
- Add boundary-aware flush logic that defers flushes mid-UTF8/grapheme sequence and avoids breaking JSON tokens across chunk boundaries.
- Update the OpenAI compatibility adapter to accept chunked partial-json sequences and reconstruct them deterministically into complete objects for clients that expect structured JSON messages (function/tool calling payloads).
- Add integration tests that replay known problematic traces (from SUP-901 incident) and validate that the streamed sequence reconstructs into valid JSON arrays/objects in the same order produced by the model.
- Add documentation and a short migration note describing compatibility behavior and the non-breaking nature of the change.

Files changed (high-level):
- redwood/api/streaming/sse_emitter.cpp: Add buffering layer, delimiter ordering changes, and boundary-aware flush helper.
- redwood/api/streaming/sse_emitter_test.py: Unit tests for partial JSON, delimiter ordering, and token-boundary behavior.
- redwood/openai_compat/streaming_adapter.go: Reassembly logic for partial-json chunks and improved event semantics mapping to OpenAI streaming.
- redwood-sdk-typescript/src/streaming.ts: Adjust client-side reconstructor to tolerate reordered data+delim sequences (backcompat).
- docs/streaming.md: Notes on SSE semantics and migration guidance for custom clients.
- perf-canary/integration/traces/fixtures/partial_json_trace.json: New test fixture derived from incident exports.
- redwood/api/streaming/README.md: small note about the bounded buffer heuristic.

Commits (high-level):
- 7e4a1b0: sse: add bounded partial-json buffer to emitter and tests
- b2c93d4: sse: normalize delimiter ordering and add ordering tests
- f1d0a77: openai_compat: reassembly for chunked partial-json and tool call payloads
- a9c2d55: sdk-ts: tolerate ordering variance in streaming reconstructor
- 3d87c9f: docs: streaming migration guide and reproduction fixture

Behavioral notes and rationale:
- The buffer approach only coalesces bytes for a given logical event; it does not attempt to re-interpret JSON beyond ensuring that brackets/strings are not obviously split mid-codepoint. We intentionally avoid deep parsing in the hot path for latency reasons; the reassembly uses lightweight heuristics and a small optional background validator for edge cases.
- To preserve latency SLOs we cap the buffer at 64KB per stream and expose a metric (sse.buffer.flush_due_to_capacity) and a config knob for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers. When the cap is reached we flush with a warning event so downstreams can handle incomplete payloads. This keeps behavior predictable under high-throughput workloads.
- The new delimiter ordering (emit data line(s) first, then the event name, then the terminating "\n\n") is documented and was chosen after testing with major OpenAI-compatible clients (node-openai, openai-python streaming harnesses). We keep the previous delimiter shape ("data: ...") so most clients do not need changes.

Testing and CI:
- Added unit tests (sse_emitter_test.py) covering partial JSON across boundaries including UTF-8 multi-byte characters and emoji sequences.
- Added integration test that replays a recorded trace that previously caused invalid JSON on the client. The trace now reconstructs into valid JSON and preserves event ordering.
- CI: linux-build/tests/lint all pass locally and on CI. A flakey test in perf-canary was fixed by making the fixture deterministic.

Compatibility and migration:
- This change is non-breaking for the vast majority of clients. Most clients will see fewer truncated JSON errors.
- For custom clients that relied on previous, non-deterministic delimiter ordering, we documented the expected sequence and provided a backwards-compatible reconstructor in the TS SDK release.

Checklist:
- [x] Add buffering & ordering code in emitter
- [x] Add unit & integration tests
- [x] Update OpenAI-compat adapter
- [x] Update SDK reconstructor (TS)
- [x] Add docs/migration note
- [x] Add metrics and config knobs for buffer cap

Related: SUP-901 (customer incident), ENG-2145 (streaming reliability epic), ENG-2180 (openai-compat adapter improvements).

ci_details: integration-tests: passed (includes replay of SUP-901 trace)
release_notes: Fixes SSE streaming framing that could produce truncated/invalid JSON in streaming responses. Improves OpenAI-compat streaming adapter and adds a bounded coalescing buffer to avoid splitting partial JSON across chunk boundaries. Non-breaking for most clients; see docs/streaming.md for migration notes.
notes_for_release_engineers: After deployment, monitor metric sse.buffer.flush_due_to_capacity and streaming.error_rate for any spikes. Default buffer cap is 64KB; customers can override via runtime config under streaming.buffer_cap_bytes. Rolling deploy is safe; the change is backwards compatible but observe client reconstructor errors for custom clients.
reproduction_steps: 1) Run perf-canary/integration/traces/fixtures/partial_json_trace.json through the emitter harness. 2) Confirm the client-side reconstructor (redwood-sdk-typescript) reconstructs valid JSON objects in the same order. 3) Run node-openai and openai-python streaming harnesses against the updated endpoint. Expected: no truncated JSON errors and event order preserved.
migration_guide: No required migration for most users. If you implement a custom SSE parser that relied on earlier delimiter ordering, update it to accept data events followed by the terminating delimiter. See docs/streaming.md for code examples and the SDK TS tolerant reconstructor.

- Bump SDK TS patch release to include reconstructor fix

notes: This PR was intentionally conservative on heavy parsing in the hot path; the reassembly heuristics are lightweight and we provide an optional validator pipeline for customers that want stricter guarantees at the cost of latency.
